brief: THE BET - take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. #100 gave the diorama a foreground and it is now the largest single object in the frame (13.8% of a 1600x950 picture, 21.7% of a 390x844 phone, measured there). Nothing lives on it, and not by oversight: grep confirms the bed CA, the item sort and the opening seed scatter all bound their y loops at LN_WALK_S (79), and catA is pinned to the lane at y = LANE_N_Y - 0.5, x -2..66. So the near roof - rows 79..WH, with a capped ridge, two WELLS, a dormer or rooflight per house at DORM_Y 85, party walls with stacks at STACK_Y 86, a parapet at PARA_Y and moss on the north pitch - has no inhabitants of any kind. Give it its own life. The town already has the tenants: birds[] land/hop/fly, and plazaBirdSpot() is the model to copy - a place-specific spot picker with its OWN roll and cap, which is exactly how #92 stopped the plaza's pigeons competing for a shared budget. catA is the second: a cat that has only ever walked the lane could come up onto the parapet after dark and walk the ridge, which is the nearest and largest thing in the night picture. MUR_ROOSTS could take a near-roof entry. And c151's other half is still open: nothing looks down the two light wells.
successLooksLike: On a wide shot at 1200x720 the near roof is somewhere the eye goes: at least one living thing is on it in a clear majority of daylit samples, counted by its own probe against a HEAD control that reads zero, and after dark the cat or a roosting bird is findable in the same band. The roof stops being the emptiest surface in the picture.
avoid: Do not widen the general birds[] roll or spawnLaneAgent to reach the roof - a spawn band is a share of a budget, so the roof needs its own source and its own cap (plazaBirdSpot is the pattern). Do not put PEOPLE on it. Do not move LN_WALK_S or change the near block's footprint: #100's roof is emergent from buildVolumes and a footprint change grows a different roof. Two traps that will bite: project() lifts z NORTHWARD ~1.15 rows per cell of height, so a bird on the ridge at row 83 can render north of the lane - price everything by its own row exactly as #100 had to for the stacks; and drawNearRoof is in the GROUND CACHE, so anything that moves must be a live overlay after the cache blit, and anything warm at night must go in a screen pass AFTER applyLight.
